_meta.eraBasis: The era of asOfA, the earlier cost observation. Cross-era pairs count once, in their starting era. This is not the production's opening era.
_meta.dateBasis: asOf describes the cost, reportedAt describes publication. Period averages use the documented period midpoint or end, explained in each source note. Neither dates nor amounts are extracted from URLs.
_meta.scope: Public amounts and source paraphrases only. No source quotations. These are research observations, never model inputs or permission to enable datedCosts. Coverage alone cannot establish no-worse recoupment categories or zero new false recoupments.
_meta.caveat: The long Phantom interval and the short Good Night budget-to-actual comparison are disclosed rather than treated as independent annual inflation measurements. More dated observations are needed in every era.

pairs.costBasis: reported weekly running costs for the original Broadway production

sourceA.note: Mackintosh's contemporary Broadway weekly running-cost statement.

sourceB.note: General manager Aaron Lustbader's current weekly cost; indexed Yahoo syndication also confirms this amount.

pairs.costBasis: fixed weekly expenses excluding royalties and percentage rent

sourceA.note: First-year average in the corrected article. February 2016 represents the midpoint of the first Broadway year, matching the researched seeds. The correction removes variable theater rent.

sourceB.note: Annual fixed-expense average for the year ended July 2017. January 2017 represents that period's midpoint, matching the researched seeds. April 2018 is the publication date, not another cost observation.

pairs.costBasis: weekly operating costs before royalties, production budget versus run average

sourceA.note: Current operating-paper budget reported during the Broadway run. This is the production's budget, not a category estimate.

sourceB.note: Financial statements give the 13-week 2025 run average plus royalties. The cost date is the run's end, not March 2026. This checks budget fidelity over the run, not a year's inflation after closing.
